question: Summarize the key differences between evaluation protocol v1 and v2.
answer: Evaluation Protocol v2 uses a 70-15-15 data split for training, validation, and testing respectively [S1] [S3]. For cross-validation, v2 employs k=5 folds and reports mean and standard deviation of fold scores [S1]. Random state is set to 42 in both protocols [S1] [S3]. The primary metric is F1 for imbalanced data and accuracy otherwise [S1].

Evaluation Protocol v2
Evaluation protocol v2 supersedes protocol v1 for all projects started in 2025. Split the data 70% training, 15% validation and 15% test. Use k = 5 folds for cross-validation and report the mean and standard deviation of the fold scores. Set random_state=42 everywhere. The test set may be used exactly once. The primary metric is F1 for imbalanced data and accuracy otherwise.

S5.title: Ml Lecture Notes
S5.text: 4. Evaluation Metrics for Classification A confusion matrix counts true positives (TP), false positives (FP), true negatives (TN) and false negatives (FN). Accuracy is (TP + TN) divided by all examples. Accuracy is misleading on imbalanced data: a model that always predicts the majority class can reach 99% accuracy while detecting nothing. Precision = TP / (TP + FP) answers "of the examples predicted positive, how many are truly positive?". Recall (sensitivity) = TP / (TP + FN) answers "of the truly positive examples, how many did we find?". The F1 score is the harmonic mean of precision and recall: 2 * precision * recall / (precision + recall). Raising the decision threshold usually increases precision and lowers recall. The ROC curve plots the true positive rate against the false positive rate across thresholds, and AUC summarizes it: 0.5 is random guessing and 1.0 is perfect ranking.
